newsitem.title: CHINA: China calls for vigilance against Medfly.
newsitem.headline: China calls for vigilance against Medfly.

text.p: China has called for greater vigilance against the Mediterranean fruit fly, warning of huge losses for fruit growers if the insect gains a presence in China's orchards, the China Daily said on Friday.

"There already is a great potential threat of an insect-caused disaster to the nation's fruit industry," the newspaper quoted an official of the China Administration of Animal and Plant Quarantine as saying.
Quarantine authorities had found six instances of fruit-fly contaminated imports at southern ports over the past few years, the newspaper said.
Last month, infested oranges were confiscated from a Belarus traveller in the northern city of Tianjin, the newspaper said.

"Once this kind of insect comes into China, it will not only cause damage to the country's fruit production but will also affect China's foreign trade," the newspaper quoted Zhao Sen, a Tianjin quarantine official, as saying.

The quarantine administration was improving inspections across China and expected better cooperation from traders and passengers in declaring agricultural products on arrival in the country, the newspaper said. It gave no further details.
Medflies lay their eggs in about 250 varieties of fruit and vegetables, destroying them.
Pete Wilson, governor of California, said in January he did not understand why Chinese authorities had refused to recognise the U.S. state as free of the Medfly.
He said this was barring access of produce from the big agricultural state to a potentially large market.
